title: Customer Resonance Priority Engine & Roadmap Lifting
creator: Nora Patel
description: Problem: We currently rely on ad-hoc signals (sales emails, CS slack, and manual PM judgment) to elevate feature requests from strategic customers. This creates opaque prioritization, inconsistent SLAs for top accounts, and last-minute roadmap changes that conflict with OKRs. Goal: Build a reproducible, transparent "Customer Resonance Score" (CRS) and a corresponding "Roadmap Lift" policy that automatically surfaces, routes, and gates incoming intake from top accounts and escalations. Scope: - Intake UI + webhook enrichment (sales/CS metadata) - CRS nightly scoring and ranking - Routing rules for PM triage and engineering fast lanes - Console dashboard view and weekly digest for GTM and execs Out of scope: full automation of releases (we will not auto-commit code changes) and contractual SLA changes (legal to decide).
acceptance_criteria: CRS is computed nightly for all accounts and available via console API
Top 20 accounts (by CRS) are flagged and appear in a dedicated dashboard
Incoming intake items linked to flagged accounts are automatically labeled and routed to the prioritized intake queue
Routing rules include clear owner assignments and SLA for response (24h triage for P0 top-account items)
At least one PM and one senior engineer approve the scoring formula and routing rules in a formal review
A demo of the dashboard and routing flow is presented to GTM and executive stakeholders with feedback captured
proposed_scoring_formula:
Customer Resonance Score (CRS) = weighted sum of signals: 
- ARR_weight * normalized(ARR) (weight 0.30) 
- PipelineVelocity_weight * normalized(new_pipeline_last_90d) (weight 0.20) 
- Escalation_weight * (num_escalations_last_30d * 0.25) (weight 0.20) 
- ProductGap_weight * normalized(number_of_product_requests / open_asks) (weight 0.15) 
- ChurnRisk_weight * normalized(churn_risk_score) (weight 0.10) 
Notes: each component normalized to 0..1 per percentile within customer set. Priority multiplier: strategic_partner_flag adds +0.10 to final score. Pseudocode: compute_percentile(signal) for each account -> apply weights -> CRS = sum(weights * percentiles) + strategic_bonus. Recompute nightly with incremental updates from CRM and CS webhooks.
mock_routing_rules: CRS >= 0.85 -> 'Top Account Triage' bucket: assign PM on-call, notify Head of Sales, create urgent review channel; SLA: PM ack within 6 hours, triage decision within 48 hours.
0.65 <= CRS < 0.85 -> 'Elevated' bucket: assign PM, notify CSM; SLA: PM ack within 24 hours, decision within 5 business days.
0.40 <= CRS < 0.65 -> 'Monitor' bucket: label and queue for regular backlog review in next roadmap cycle.
CRS < 0.40 -> 'Standard' intake: route to product backlog with no special SLAs.
metrics_to_track: # of intake items flagged as Top (weekly)
% of Top-account requests resulting in roadmap commitment within 2 cycles
Customer satisfaction (post-response CSAT) for escalated items
False positive rate: percent of flagged items with low business impact after review

risks: Overfitting to historical ARR could bias against high-growth but low-current-ARR accounts.
Incomplete or delayed CRM/CS data will skew nightly CRS computations.
GTM teams may game signals if CRS directly influences sales compensation; mitigated by transparency and audit logs.
Automation of routing could overload on-call PMs if thresholds are too permissive.

Design spec and intake UI changes
Pilot report summarizing outcome and recommended threshold adjustments

notes: UX: intake form should surface account CRS and explain why the item was flagged (transparency).
Ops: make the nightly job idempotent and provide delta-only recompute to reduce cost.
Governance: keep an audit trail of manual overrides with justification for later review.
Next steps after pilot: consider exposing per-feature lift score to Sales for negotiation conversations.
